newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks rebound in weekly trade.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks rebound in weekly trade.

text.p: Cyprus shares rose sharply during the week with gains made in most of the sectoral indices, led by stocks in the banking sector.

The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) general index, which is set at 100 points, closed at 84.80, gaining 1.21 percent from last Friday's close of 83.78. Earlier this week the market gained 1.13 percent in one trading session.
Gains of two percent were posted in the banking sub index, which closed at 93.99 from 92.14 last week.

CISCO, the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation, said in its weekly report that the success of the Bank of Cyprus in its issue of a convertible 40 million pound bond issue brought a renewed air of confidence to the CSE.

The issue, listed on the Luxembourg stock exchange, had been over subscribed by investors 3.6 times. Later this month the bank is due to offer convertible bonds worth 10 million pounds to existing bank shareholders.

Bank of Cyprus fully paid closed at 354.5, gaining nine cents over last week's close of 345.5. Fully-paid shares in the Cyprus Popular Bank stood at 335, adding 4.5 cents from its closing figure last week of 330.5.
Fully paid shares of Hellenic Bank gained three cents to close at 272, while the Universal Savings Bank closed at 136, half a cent down from last week.
Shares in Keo, the Cypriot wine and beer producer, fell to 107.5, a year low after closing last Friday at 1.12.
On Tuesday the company announced losses before tax of 393,000 pounds in the first half of the year, blaming the decline on a drop in tourism, on which it depends for the bulk of its revenue.

The index of the insurance sector closed at 62.12, up from 61.27 last week. Universal Life Insurance closed down by one cent, to 379. Paneuropean Insurance fully paid closed with gains of 4.5 cents to 143. Fully paid shares in subsidiary Interamerican Insurance closed 3.5 cents up at 107.5.
Shares in the Cyprus Tourism Development Company, which announced a pretax loss of 110,322 pounds in its H1 results on Friday, closed at 872.5, down 17.5 cents from last week.
Shares in national carrier Cyprus Airways closed unchanged 42 cents, losing 2.5 cents from last week.
